tagline: The Stanford NLP Group is a leading academic research group whose open software, including CoreNLP, GloVe, Stanza and DSPy, underpins much of modern language technology.
about: The Stanford NLP Group was started in 2000 by Christopher Manning, who held a joint appointment in linguistics and computer science. It grew to include faculty such as Dan Jurafsky, who arrived in 2004, and Percy Liang, who joined in 2012. The group is part of Stanford University and brings together linguists and computer scientists.

Its software history begins with the Stanford Parser, released as open source in December 2002, and the first unified CoreNLP package appeared on 1 November 2010. Later releases include GloVe word vectors, the Python library Stanza for many human languages, and the DSPy framework for programming rather than prompting language models.
The group publishes code, data and papers openly, and its GitHub organization is among the most widely used sources of NLP tooling for researchers, students and industry engineers.
mission: To advance the computational understanding of human language and to share research software and datasets that others can build on.

tagline: StepFun is a Shanghai foundation-model company that has released open-weight language, speech and video models under permissive licenses.
about: StepFun, formally Shanghai Jieyue Xingchen Intelligent Technology, was founded in April 2023 by Jiang Daxin, Zhu Yibo and Jiao Binxing, all formerly of Microsoft. It is often counted among China's six leading foundation-model startups, and its investors include Tencent and Qiming Venture Partners.

The company builds large language, multimodal, image, video and audio models. Step-2, a trillion-parameter model, appeared in 2024, and it open-sourced Step-Video-T2V and Step-Audio in February 2025 together with Geely.

Its recent open releases, Step 3.5 Flash in February 2026 and Step 3.7 Flash in May 2026, use the Apache 2.0 license. Its latest preview model, Step 5, is closed-weight, so openness varies by release.
mission: StepFun states an aim of building frontier multimodal models and making many of them available to developers.

tagline: Stockmark is a Tokyo company that has released large Japanese-language models, including the 100-billion-parameter Stockmark-100b, under permissive licenses.
about: Stockmark is a Japanese company focused on business information and language models. Its co-founder and CTO is Kosuke Arima, and its researchers publish models on Hugging Face under the stockmark organization.

Stockmark-100b is a 100-billion-parameter model pretrained from scratch on about 910 billion tokens of Japanese and English text and released under the MIT license. The company later released Stockmark-2-100B-Instruct and a multimodal Stockmark-2-VL-100B, both developed under Japan's GENIAC program.
The models target Japanese business use, with a stated focus on reducing hallucination in domain questions.
mission: Stockmark aims to provide Japanese-first language models that companies can run and adapt, with open weights.

tagline: Swallow is a Japanese LLM project at the Institute of Science Tokyo that continually pretrains open models to give them strong Japanese ability.
about: Swallow is led by researchers in the Okazaki and Yokota laboratories at the Institute of Science Tokyo, together with the National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST). Naoaki Okazaki leads the project and the pre-training corpus team, Rio Yokota leads LLM training, and Sakae Mizuki leads instruction tuning and evaluation.

The project adapts existing open models such as Llama, Mistral, Gemma, Qwen and gpt-oss to Japanese through continual pretraining and instruction tuning. Its model list runs from the first Swallow models to Llama 3.3 Swallow 70B, Qwen3 Swallow and GPT-OSS Swallow.
Weights are published on Hugging Face under the tokyotech-llm organization, and the project documents its corpus and evaluation work for the Japanese community.
mission: Swallow aims to build and openly release Japanese large language models and the corpora and evaluation methods needed to improve them.

tagline: The Swiss AI Initiative is a national ETH Zurich and EPFL effort that trained the fully open Apertus language models on the Alps supercomputer.
about: The Swiss AI Initiative started in December 2023, seeded with more than 10 million GPU hours on the Alps system run by CSCS and a CHF 20 million grant from the ETH Domain. It is run with the ETH AI Center and the EPFL AI Center, with Swisscom as strategic partner.

Its main output is Apertus, released on 2 September 2025 in 8B and 70B sizes under Apache 2.0. Apertus was trained on over 1,800 languages and designed to follow European copyright law, with an emphasis on transparency and auditability.
An Apertus 1.5 release is listed for July 2026.
mission: The initiative aims to build transparent, sovereign foundation models for Switzerland and to share them with the wider research community.

tagline: TAIDE is a Taiwanese government-backed project releasing open Traditional Chinese language models for trustworthy local use.
about: TAIDE, the Trustworthy AI Dialogue Engine, launched on 27 April 2023. The National Science and Technology Council acts as guiding agency, and the National Institutes of Applied Research implements the work.

The project has released the TAIDE-LX-7B model in 2024, Llama 3 and Llama 3.1 based 8B chat models, and Gemma 3 based 12B chat models in 2025 and 2026. A small embedding model, Embeddinggemma-GTAIDE-300m, appeared in 2026.
Its models are intended to serve Traditional Chinese users and Taiwanese institutions.
mission: TAIDE aims to provide a trustworthy Traditional Chinese language model base for Taiwan's public and private sectors.

about: TartuNLP is a natural language processing group at the University of Tartu in Estonia. Its site presents work on Estonian language models, machine translation and speech synthesis.
Named projects include Llammas, an Estonian-adapted Llama model, EstBERT, and the Neurotõlge translation service. Code and models are published through the TartuNLP GitHub organization.
mission: The group works to provide open language technology for Estonian and related smaller languages.

tagline: Te Hiku Media is a Māori iwi media organization in Kaitaia that builds te reo Māori speech technology under Māori data sovereignty.
about: Te Hiku Media, formally Te Reo Irirangi o Te Hiku o Te Ika, is an iwi radio and media organization in Kaitaia whose site dates its roots to 1991. It runs Te Hiku Tech, which builds tools for te reo Māori.

Its Kōrero Māori campaign collected labelled speech under the Kaitiakitanga License, which restricts use of the data to the benefit of Māori people. The organization reported a speech recognizer for te reo Māori built with DeepSpeech, with accuracy of about 92 percent.
All content on its site is covered by the same licence, and contributors retain ownership of their data.
mission: Te Hiku Media aims to revitalize te reo Māori with technology that Māori communities own and control.

tagline: TII is Abu Dhabi's government-funded research institute and the publisher of the Falcon open language models.
about: The Technology Innovation Institute is part of the Advanced Technology Research Council of the Abu Dhabi government. It works across AI, quantum computing, robotics, cryptography and other fields, and its Artificial Intelligence and Digital Science Research Center builds the Falcon models.

Falcon 40B and 7B were released in 2023, followed by Falcon 180B in September 2023, Falcon 2 11B in May 2024 and Falcon 3 in December 2024. Later work includes the hybrid Falcon-H1 family and Falcon-H1 Arabic in January 2026.
TII is state funded, so its openness follows its license choices per release.
mission: TII aims to build sovereign, efficient AI models and release them for the global research community.

tagline: The Alan Turing Institute is the UK's national institute for data science and AI, which maintains a large body of open research software.
about: The Alan Turing Institute was founded in 2015 as the UK's national institute for data science, and AI was added to its remit in 2017. It is named after Alan Turing and is largely government funded.
Its researchers and engineers publish many open repositories on GitHub. Since 2025 the institute has focused on defence and national security at the government's request.
In May 2026 George Williamson, previously of HMGCC, was named chief executive.
mission: The institute's stated direction is now to serve UK sovereign capability in AI, defence and security.

tagline: Tilde is a Latvian language technology company that trained TildeOpen, an open 30B model covering 34 European languages.
about: Tilde is a language technology company based in Latvia that builds machine translation and language tools. In 2024 it won the European Commission's Large AI Grand Challenge, which awarded 2 million GPU hours on the LUMI supercomputer.

On that compute it trained TildeOpen LLM, a 30B dense decoder-only model on the Llama 3 architecture, trained on 2 trillion tokens for 34 European languages. It was released in October 2025 on Hugging Face under CC BY 4.0.
A technical report presented at LREC 2026 describes the curriculum learning used to give lower-resource languages equitable representation.
mission: Tilde aims to give smaller European languages an open model that serves them as well as large ones.

about: Together AI was founded by Vipul Ved Prakash, Ce Zhang, Chris Ré and Percy Liang, with Tri Dao joining as chief scientist in July 2023. It combines a commercial inference cloud with an open research group.
In April 2023 it released RedPajama, a 1.2 trillion token pre-training dataset reproducing the LLaMA recipe, and later the 30 trillion token RedPajama-V2. It announced FlashAttention-2 in July 2023.
Its research outputs are open, but the company's main business is a paid platform.
mission: Together aims to provide an open, high-performance platform for building with open-source models.

tagline: Transluce is a nonprofit AI research lab building open tools to understand and oversee AI systems.
about: Transluce was co-founded in 2024 by Jacob Steinhardt and Sarah Schwettmann, with Steinhardt on leave from UC Berkeley and Schwettmann previously at MIT CSAIL. It describes itself as a nonprofit that builds open, scalable tools for understanding frontier AI.

It launched publicly on 23 October 2024 with neuron-description tools, Monitor and investigator agents. It later released Docent, which analyzes agent transcripts to find bugs and unexpected behaviour and is used by more than 25 organizations.
mission: Transluce aims to enable scalable, democratic oversight of AI through open tooling.

It open-sourced the preview Trillion-7B model in March 2025 and Tri-21B in July 2025, a model trained from scratch that runs on a single GPU. Tri 21B Think, adding reinforcement learning for reasoning, followed in February 2026.

Its Heron family of vision-language models, supported by Japan's GENIAC program, includes the Heron-NVILA-Lite 15B, 2B and 1B models. In March 2026 it reported Japan's first real-time public-road driving controlled by a vision-language-action model.

With Silo AI's SiloGen it built the Poro and Viking models on the LUMI supercomputer. Viking, released in 2024 in 7B, 13B and 33B sizes, covers Danish, Finnish, Norwegian, Icelandic, Swedish, English and code and is Apache 2.0 licensed.
mission: The group aims to produce open language resources and models for Finnish and the Nordic languages.

It created Sentence-BERT, the Sentence Transformers library, with Nils Reimers in 2019, and develops AdapterHub. In October 2025 maintenance of Sentence Transformers passed to Hugging Face under Apache 2.0.
